sections.content:
The creature is idle at (32,56), and no new sockets have appeared. In other words, the creature is waiting. The pipe has 2 sockets (24,52) and (32,52).
Hypothesis: the pipe has 4 slots, and the creature needs to bring 4 sockets. Available sockets: D (12,32) can be reached by the creature; A, B, C are on the left side — the player has to bring them to the creature… but the player can't cross the band.
Wait a moment. Maybe the player can pick up A, B, C, and when the player holds them, the creature… no, that's not it.
Another idea: maybe the player's job is to bring the left-side sockets to the edge of the band, and the creature picks them up from the right side of the band?? The player can't place them on the right side of the band.
Hmm, wait. Let me reconsider the band. The band is a lattice of 'g' cells. The player (4x4) is blocked. But what about a carried object? In level 2, the player carried S1 above their head, and the creature picked it up. Here, maybe the player carries a socket to the edge of the band, and the creature… no, the creature is on the opposite side.
Let me think from another angle: maybe the pipe's slots fill up automatically over time, or when the creature is nearby, and the creature just needs to be at the pipe. 2 out of 4 are filled. The remaining 2 might be D and…?
Actually, wait: maybe the pipe's slots correspond to the band's sockets (D, E) + something else. E is already docked (24,52). (32,52) — what is this? Maybe when the creature docked E, a "copy" appeared… or (32,52) is where the creature docked E (row 32 = the creature's row), and (24,52) is…
Let me look at the image again: the pipe (rows 24-39, columns 52-55) has a socket with a gem at rows 24-27, and a socket with a gem at rows 32-35. The creature is at (32-35, 56-59).
So both docked sockets have gems (blue b inside).
Total sockets in the level: 5 (A, B, C, D, E). E is docked. If the pipe has 4 slots, we need 4 sockets: E, D, + 2 of {A, B, C}?
The player has to deliver A, B, C somehow. Since the player can't cross the band…
Oh, wait. Maybe I've been thinking about it backwards: maybe the player can cross the band, but only when not holding anything… no, the player was blocked while empty-handed.
Hmm, let me re-verify whether the player was really blocked. The player moved right 7 times: 16→28. Let me count the player's movement speed: in level 2, the player moved 4 columns per action. 7 actions: if all succeeded, 16+28=44. The player is at 28 → 3 successes, 4 blocks. Yes, blocked.
But wait — the player's rows at that time were 36-39. The diagonal cells in rows 36-39: (36,32), (37,33), (38,34), (39,35). The player's target cell (36-39, 32-35) contains all 4 diagonal cells → blocked.
What if the player is at rows 33-36? Diagonal cells: (33,35), (34,32), (35,33), (36,34). The player's target (33-36, 32-35) contains all 4 → blocked.
Any 4x4 window within columns 32-35 contains 4 diagonal cells → always blocked. Confirmed impassable.
So the left and right sides are separated. The creature can only handle the right-side/band sockets (D, E). The player can only handle the left-side sockets (A, B, C).
The pipe is on the right side. So the left-side sockets can never reach the pipe… unless the goal doesn't require them to!
Maybe the goal is: dock all the sockets the creature can reach (D, E) — but 2 are already docked, and D is still there.
Or: maybe the pipe's slots fill up when the creature touches the pipe, and the creature needs to touch it 4 times? 2 are filled. The creature is idle at (32,56) — adjacent to the pipe (the pipe is at columns 52-55? The pipe's frame b is at column 52… wait, the pipe: b 44 (24,52)-(39,52) is column 52, g 84 (25,53)-(38,53) is column 53. So the pipe is only 2 columns wide (52-53)! But the docked sockets are at (24,52) and (32,52) — 4x4 sockets at columns 52-55, overlapping with the pipe's columns 52-53.
Hmm, the docked socket at (24,52) spans columns 52-55 — extending to the right of the pipe.
The creature is at (32,56): columns 56-59.
So the pipe is a 2-column vertical strip, and the sockets dock to its left?? No — the sockets are at columns 52-55, and the pipe is at columns 52-53. The sockets overlap with the pipe.
I think the pipe is a "goal zone" (like the bar in level 2), and the creature docks sockets there. The creature is idle, waiting for… something.
Maybe the creature is waiting for the player to bring a socket to the band! The player carries A/B/C to the left edge of the band, and… the creature picks it up from the right edge of the band? The player can't place it on the right side.
Or: when the player carries a socket adjacent to the band, the socket passes through the band (like a wormhole)?
Let me test: the player picks up B (20-23, 20-23). Player is at (32-35, 28-31). Move to (20-23, 24-27) (right of B), and try SPACE (side pickup failed on E… but E is inside the band; B is in open space — maybe side pickup works in open space? In level 2, the player picked up from above).
Let me try: the player goes below B: (24-27, 20-23), SPACE. If pickup works from below, carry B to the band's edge (24-27, 28-31) and see what happens.
Path: player (32-35, 28-31) → up to (28-31, 28-31) → up to (24-27, 28-31) → left to (24-27, 24-27) → left to (24-27, 20-23) (below B) → SPACE.
That's 5 moves + SPACE. Let me execute and observe.
